page0.text:
I can't allow myself to die here.
It's two meters to the door.
I can escape in a single bound.
The problem is that Rider can close in on me faster than I can leap back.

page1.text:
"..."
I can't tell if there's anger or disappointment behind Rider's bloodlust.
Maybe it's just the poor lighting in the shed, but standing in the dark, she reminds me of a giant snake about to strike its prey.

page2.text:
"—, —"
I focus on predicting when the snake will strike.
"...Haah...!"
I dodge a dagger before I jump back.

page3.text:
"I made it...!"
I feel a little excited as I run into the yard.
My heartbeat rises with the exhilaration of avoiding Rider's daggers and taking the opportunity to escape, when she's stronger than me.

page4.text:
But my happiness ends there.
The fight has just begun. I need to find some way to beat Rider, or else...

page5.text:
"...Huh?"
Nobody's chasing me...?
Rider slowly emerges from the shed.
"...You have lost my interest. You cannot kill Sakura with your meager skills. I don't even need to finish you off."
Then, she vanishes into the night as suddenly as she appeared.

page6.text:
"..."
Rider's presence fades away.
She must have left the house.
Her bloodlust is gone, and it doesn't seem like it'll ever return.
